summary: Defines a mobility option that lets Mobile IPv6 nodes identify themselves using something other than their home address, such as an NAI, an FQDN, an IMSI, or an MSISDN. It can be used in messages carrying a mobility header. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: Mobile IPv6 normally identifies a device by its home address. This document adds a way for the device to also say "I am user@realm", so the network can check the account instead of the address. It is a small option added to the mobility header, with room for other kinds of name later.

what is mn-nai in mobile ipv6
how does mobile ipv6 identify a node by nai
subtitle: A Mobile IPv6 option that lets a mobile node identify itself with a name such as a user@realm NAI instead of only its home address.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv6 identifies a moving device by its IPv6 home address, but the network often needs to identify it by the account it is billed to, its subscriber identity or an application-specific name.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines a new option for the Mobile IPv6 mobility header. Its subtype field says which kind of identifier is carried; one subtype is defined, carrying a Network Access Identifier in the form user@realm.
tldr.outcome: The option can be used for authentication through existing AAA infrastructure, for dynamic allocation of a mobility anchor point, and for dynamic allocation of a home address, and it is placed before any authentication option in the message.

today: RFC 4283 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It adds one option to the Mobile IPv6 mobility header defined in RFC 3775, and it is designed to work alongside the Mobile IPv6 authentication option in RFC 4285.

sections.title: Why a Node Needs Another Identifier
sections.content:
The base specification of Mobile IPv6 identifies mobility entities using an IPv6 address. It is essential to have a mechanism whereby mobility entities can be identified using other identifiers, for example a Network Access Identifier, an International Mobile Station Identifier, or an application or deployment specific opaque identifier.

The capability to identify a mobility entity through identifiers other than the IPv6 address can be used for several functions: authentication and authorization using an existing AAA infrastructure or via a Home Location Register and Authentication Center, dynamic allocation of a mobility anchor point, and dynamic allocation of a home address.

The document defines an option with a subtype number that denotes a specific type of identifier. One instance of the subtype, the NAI, is defined. It is anticipated that other identifiers will be defined for use in the mobility header in the future.

This option SHOULD be used when Internet Key Exchange and IPsec are not used for protecting binding updates or binding acknowledgements. It is typically used with the Mobile IPv6 authentication option, but the option may be used independently, for example to provide accounting and billing services.
sections.plainLanguage: An address says where a device is; a name says whose account it is. The network often needs the second one, because that is what the billing system, the subscriber database and the home address allocator all work with.

sections.title: The Mobile Node Identifier Option
sections.content:
The Mobile Node Identifier option is a new optional data field carried in the Mobile IPv6 messages that include the mobility header. Various forms of identifier can be used to identify a mobile node; two examples given are a Network Access Identifier and an opaque identifier applicable to a particular application. The Subtype field in the option defines the specific type of identifier, and it is used to interpret the identifier that follows.

The option has four fields. Option Type is MN-ID-OPTION-TYPE, assigned the value 8 by IANA, and is an 8-bit identifier of the type of mobility option. Option Length is an 8-bit unsigned integer representing the length in octets of the Subtype and Identifier fields. Subtype defines the specific type of identifier included in the Identifier field. Identifier is a variable length identifier of the type specified by the Subtype field.

The option does not have any alignment requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: The option is four pieces: a fixed number saying what kind of option this is, a length, a second number saying what kind of name follows, and the name itself. The name can be any length.

sections.title: The NAI Subtype
sections.content:
The MN-NAI mobility option uses the general format of the Mobile Node Identifier option, with the subtype value of 1, and is used to identify the mobile node.

The identifier it carries has the form user@realm, as defined for the Network Access Identifier. This option MUST be implemented by the entities implementing this specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The one identifier defined here is the subscriber name in the form user@realm, the same shape used for roaming logins. Every implementation of this specification has to support it.

sections.title: Where the Option Appears
sections.content: When present, the Mobile Node Identifier option MUST appear before any authentication-related option in a message containing a mobility header.
sections.plainLanguage: The name goes in the message ahead of any authentication option, so that the receiving side knows who is speaking before it checks the credentials.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Mobile IPv6 already contains one mechanism for identifying mobile nodes, the Home Address option. The vulnerabilities of the new option defined in this document are therefore similar to those that already exist for Mobile IPv6. In particular, the use of a permanent, stable identifier may compromise the privacy of the user, making it possible to track a particular device or user as it moves through different locations.

Because the Mobile Node Identifier option reveals the home affiliation of a user, it may assist an attacker in determining the identity of the user, help the attacker in targeting specific victims, or assist in further probing of the username space. These vulnerabilities can be addressed through several mechanisms. Traffic can be encrypted at the link layer, so that other users on the same link do not see the identifiers, though this does not help against attackers on the rest of the path between the mobile node and its home agent. The whole packet can be encrypted, for example when using IPsec to protect communications with the home agent. Or an authentication mechanism can be used that enables the use of privacy NAIs, that is, temporary, changing pseudonyms as identifiers.

In any case, the identifier option is only needed on the first registration at the home agent, and subsequent registrations can use the home address, so the window of privacy vulnerability is reduced compared with the base Mobile IPv6 specification. The document is also part of a solution to allow dynamic home addresses to be used, which is an improvement to privacy as well, and it affects both communications with the home agent and the correspondent nodes, both of which have to be told the home address.
sections.plainLanguage: A permanent identifier is trackable, so the document lists ways to limit that: encrypt the link, encrypt the whole packet, or use a name that changes. The exposure is also short, because the identifier is only needed the first time a device registers with its home agent.

sections.title: Registry Entries
sections.content:
Values for new mobility options must be assigned from the Mobile IPv6 numbering space. IANA has assigned the value 8 for the MN-ID-OPTION-TYPE.

IANA has also created a new namespace for the subtype field of the Mobile Node Identifier option. The currently allocated value is the NAI, defined in RFC 4282. New values for this namespace can be allocated using Standards Action.
sections.plainLanguage: The option gets a number of 8, and the list of identifier kinds is a fresh registry with one entry so far, so more kinds of name can be added later.

fields.name: Option Type
fields.desc: MN-ID-OPTION-TYPE, assigned the value 8 by IANA.

fields.name: Option Length
fields.desc: The length in octets of the Subtype and Identifier fields.

fields.name: Subtype
fields.desc: Defines the specific type of identifier included in the Identifier field.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.desc: A variable length identifier of the type specified by the Subtype field.

viz.caption: WHAT THE EXTRA IDENTIFIER CAN BE USED FOR

items.title: Authentication and authorization
items.text: Use an existing AAA infrastructure, or a Home Location Register and Authentication Center.

items.title: Choosing a mobility anchor point
items.text: Allocate the anchor point dynamically, once the node's identity is known.

items.title: Choosing a home address
items.text: Allocate the home address dynamically rather than assigning one in advance.

items.title: Accounting and billing
items.text: The option may be used on its own, without any authentication option.

viz.caption: WAYS TO LIMIT THE PRIVACY EXPOSURE

items.title: Encrypt the link
items.text: Other users on the same link do not see the identifiers, though attackers further along the path still do.

items.title: Encrypt the whole packet
items.text: For example with IPsec protecting communications with the home agent.

items.title: Use a changing name
items.text: An authentication mechanism that permits privacy NAIs, that is, temporary pseudonyms.

items.title: Use it only once
items.text: The identifier is needed only on the first registration at the home agent; later registrations can use the home address.
